aliases: build a robot that navigates itself
summary: Build a small ground rover that maps its surroundings with a LiDAR and navigates on its own: robotics middleware ties it together, a motor driver moves it, a laser scanner senses the world, SLAM builds a live map, and a navigation stack plans and drives the path. Software is free/OSS; the hardware is an orderable kit.

capabilities.capability: motor driver control library + driver board
capabilities.query: gpiozero motor driver tb6612 l298n raspberry pi
rplidar lidar driver ros scan perception

build_steps.title: Build the rolling base
build_steps.detail: Assemble the 4WD chassis kit, mount the Raspberry Pi 5, wire the drive motors to the TB6612/L298N motor driver, and mount the RPLIDAR on top with a clear 360° view.
uses: motor driver control library + driver board

build_steps.title: Install the middleware
build_steps.detail: Install ROS 2 on the Pi. Verify you can command the motors (gpiozero test) and see LiDAR scans (rplidar_ros) as ROS topics.
uses: motor driver control library + driver board

build_steps.title: Map with SLAM
build_steps.detail: Run slam_toolbox and drive the rover around; it builds a live occupancy map from the LiDAR scans. Save the map.

build_steps.title: Navigate autonomously
build_steps.detail: Bring up Nav2 with the saved map, set a goal pose, and let the planner + controller drive the rover there while avoiding obstacles.

safety: A self-driving robot can run into people, pets, or stairs. Test at low speed in a bounded area first, keep a wireless e-stop / kill switch, and never run navigation unattended near a drop.
